correctness.rationale: For ||x||=1, ||y||=r<=1, convexity and the James-unit-vector condition select a sign with ||x±y||<=1+r(J-1). The exact square identity (1+(J-1)^2)(1+r^2)-(1+r(J-1))^2=(r-(J-1))^2 gives the global inequality. On N(s,t)=max(|s|,|t|,|s-t|), the dihedral isometries reduce all unit pairs to four hexagonal edge classes and prove J=3/2. Explicit vectors p=(1,0), q=(-1/4,-1/2) have ||p||=1,||q||=1/2,||p±q||=5/4; therefore quotient=5/4. Independently checked this witness using Fraction; inspected exact edge-class expressions and verify.py. Finite rational grid is corroboration, not a proof of continuum exhaustiveness; the analytical edge reductions prove that.
residual_risks: Only sharpness at James value 3/2 is established, not equality for every attainable J nor classification of all equality spaces.

Kato--Maligranda--Takahashi (2001) proves weaker C_NJ comparison; 2026 isosceles-orthogonal paper has a formally identical envelope for a different constrained invariant and does not imply the unrestricted theorem. value.rationale: A sharp functional relation between two standard Banach-space geometric invariants is directly useful when the James constant is known and the unrestricted minimum-type constant is not; the affine-regular hexagon realizes its optimal coefficient at a natural intermediate James value. Exact edge witness and equality at J=3/2 make the bound substantive rather than a normalization check, though its proof is short and does not give a pointwise optimal envelope at all J.
residual_risks: No classification of James values at which the envelope is attained; the sharpness is verified at J=3/2 only.

final_claim: For every real Banach space dim>=2, unrestricted Takahashi C_{-infinity}(X) <= 1+(J(X)-1)^2; Day-James hexagon has J=3/2 and C_{-infinity}=5/4, giving pointwise sharpness at J=3/2.
limitations: Only sharpness at James value 3/2 is established, not equality for every attainable J nor classification of all equality spaces.
